answer: In a tundra fire-monitoring market, agents reporting an ember must attach proof of fresh computational work. Hash the round seed, voting key and nonce until the digest meets a public target; validators check it cheaply and count each proof once. An echo of the same report under new keys earns no free weight: votes track verified work, not account count. A thousand aliases sharing one computing budget gain no advantage; more influence needs more computation and power. Cheap electricity and specialized chips remain advantages.
